name: Sister (Suite Notaro)
tagline: Wolters Kluwer's practice management suite for Italian notaries, covering deeds, registries and filings.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: Sister is not really software in the sense this site usually judges, it is a compliance conduit. An Italian notary's day is deed templates, repertorio and index registers, stamp duty and registration tax math, and electronic filings to Agenzia delle Entrate, the Registro Imprese and the Consiglio Nazionale del Notariato, all with legally mandated formats and digital signature chains. You can absolutely build a document generator and a searchable deed archive in a session. What you cannot build is the certified filing pipeline, the accepted-by-the-registry XML, or the liability cover when a submission bounces. A one-shot replacement here is not a cost saving, it is a professional risk.
coreLoopDIY: A local deed template engine plus a searchable register: fill a form, merge into a Word or PDF deed, log it in a numbered repertorio with parties, dates and amounts, and export CSV for whoever actually does the filing.
requirements: Node 20 and a local SQLite file
Docx templates you author yourself for each deed type
Someone who actually knows Italian notarial formalities to review the templates
A real, certified filing channel for anything that leaves the office
whatYouLose: Certified electronic filing to Agenzia delle Entrate, Registro Imprese and the notarial archives
Maintained deed and clause templates that track changes in Italian law
Automatic calculation of registration tax, mortgage tax and stamp duty at current rates
Digital signature and marca temporale integration that registries accept
Vendor liability, support and the audit trail an inspection expects
moatNotes: The product is glue between one profession and several state registries. The glue is the product.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a notary in Italy is a public official and a rejected or malformed filing is a professional problem, not a support ticket. The suite exists so nobody in the office has to know the current XML schema for a registration, the current tax tables, or which signature format the registry accepts this year. Paying a large vendor to track all of that, and to be the one who fixes it when it changes, is cheaper than the alternative. Nobody buys this for the UI.
notes: The document generator is a weekend; the filings are not. The moat is compliance: certified pipes into Italian state registries plus templates that change whenever the law does.
prompt:
Build a local-only deed drafting and register tool for a small Italian notary office. Do not attempt any real filing, signing or tax submission.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Node 20, TypeScript, Fastify for the API
- SQLite via better-sqlite3, single file at ./data/studio.db
- Server-rendered HTML with Eta templates, plain CSS, no SPA framework
- docxtemplater plus pizzip for document generation
- Run with: npm run dev, served on http://localhost:5173

Data model:
- parties: id, type (persona_fisica or persona_giuridica), name, codice_fiscale or partita_iva, birth data, address, notes
- acts: id, repertorio_number (auto increment, unique, never reused), raccolta_number, act_type, date, title, value_eur, notes, status (draft, signed, archived)
- act_parties: join table with a role field (venditore, acquirente, socio, mandante, etc)
- attachments: id, act_id, filename, stored path under ./data/files
- templates: id, act_type, label, docx path under ./templates

Features, all in scope:
1. CRUD for parties with search by name and codice fiscale.
2. CRUD for acts. Creating an act assigns the next repertorio number inside a transaction so numbers never collide.
3. Attach parties to an act with roles.
4. Pick a docx template for the act type, merge party and act fields, download the generated .docx. Ship two example templates with placeholder text clearly marked as NOT LEGAL TEXT.
5. Repertorio view: a filterable, date-ordered table of all acts, printable, with CSV export including repertorio number, date, act type, parties, declared value.
6. Full text search across acts and parties.
7. Nightly-ish backup command: npm run backup copies the db and files folder into ./backups with a timestamp.

Explicitly out of scope, and say so in the README:
- No electronic filing to Agenzia delle Entrate, Registro Imprese, or notarial archives
- No digital signature, no marca temporale, no PAdES or CAdES
- No registration tax, mortgage tax or stamp duty calculation
- No multi user auth, no cloud, no telemetry, no analytics

Security and config: single operator on localhost, no login. Any config goes in .env read via process.env, ship .env.example. Never commit ./data.

Write a README that states in the first paragraph that this is an internal drafting and register aid, that all legal text and all filings remain the responsibility of the notary, and that it is not a substitute for a certified practice management system. Seed the db with three fake parties and two fake acts so the UI is not empty on first run.
